subject: economics
title: Repair spending in a town with idle capacity
stem: A government brings forward a funded school-repair programme in a region with unemployed construction workers. It pays contractors directly. The central bank leaves interest rates unchanged. Some building materials are imported and contractors cannot begin every repair immediately. The case is constructed.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the component of aggregate demand directly affected and explain why a payment for a repair is classified there.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using an AD/AS diagram, explain the likely short-run effect on real output where spare capacity exists.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the increase in domestic output in the first quarter could be smaller than the announced budget.

steps.text: The government purchases a currently produced service; this is not a transfer payment to households.
Label the price level and real output axes and show the initial AD and SRAS curves.
Show AD shifting right as government purchases increase.
Indicate a higher equilibrium real output.
Spare workers and equipment allow production to respond; do not award a price-only explanation.
Imported inputs mean some of the extra demand falls on foreign production.
Payments or work scheduled later do not generate the full planned demand or output in the first quarter.

verification.method: First-assessment 2022, Unit 3.6; review of case assumptions, model and mark allocation.
verification.notes: Shared SL/HL fiscal policy. This is a data-response exercise, not a complete paper. All evidence is constructed. Alternative well-supported analyses are accepted.

subject: economics
title: One price rise, two fiscal diagnoses
stem: In two constructed economies the annual inflation rate is 6%. In L, firms report full order books, extensive overtime and difficulty hiring. In M, a crop failure raised food prices while factories report cancelled orders. Both governments propose the same cut in discretionary purchases; neither central bank changes interest rates.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain the direction of the initial change in aggregate demand if either government makes the cut.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why the proposal may ease inflationary pressure in L.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the evidence from M to explain a cost of applying the same response there.

steps.text: Government purchases are a component of aggregate demand.
Holding other components constant, lower government purchases shift AD left.
Full order books and hiring difficulties suggest demand is pressing against productive capacity.
Reduced demand eases competition for scarce labour and output.
The price level is lower than it otherwise would be, or demand-driven inflationary pressure is reduced; the price level need not fall year on year.
The crop failure indicates an adverse supply disturbance; cancelled orders do not suggest excess factory demand.
Cutting purchases does not restore crop supply.
Weaker demand can further reduce real output and employment. Accept a qualified trade-off rather than a claim that demand policy cannot affect prices at all.

verification.method: First-assessment 2022, Unit 3.6; review of case assumptions, model and mark allocation.
verification.notes: Shared SL/HL fiscal policy. This is a data-response exercise, not a complete paper. All evidence is constructed. Alternative well-supported analyses are accepted.
